guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / moving and handling
title: Back pain requiring wheelchair assistance
setting: Local event. Elderly patient suffered moderate back pain lifting grandchild, needs help getting into a wheelchair to go to the toilet.
verdictExplanation: Alert, responsive, stable observations. Safe transfer of an elderly patient with back pain. Not sick: follow safe moving and handling guidelines.

shared.danger: Limited space in the bathroom, crowds and obstacles

history.history: Injured back lifting grandchild 10 minutes ago, currently resting and awaiting advice
history.additional: Needs to use the toilet urgently

followUp.question: Which of the following symptoms, if reported by this patient, is a 'red flag' that requires immediate escalation?

options.text: Difficulty with bowel or bladder control
Pain that worsens slightly when moving
Mild muscle spasms in the lower back

followUp.explanation: Difficulty with bowel or bladder control is a red flag for serious conditions such as cauda equina syndrome and requires immediate escalation. The other symptoms are typical for mechanical back pain.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Explain the transfer, lock brakes, assist patient. Reassure during transfer.
levelFlags.erNotes: Ensure wheelchair is clean. Explain procedure, gain consent. Lock brakes. Assist to transfer, secure footplates and lap belt.
